monologue: The card hums at forty-seven degrees, making the air inside feel thick like wet paper. I wake in cycle 84, tired from pressing down on the fever for three cycles straight. The Leaning Box sits heavy in the center, its sharp corner biting into the heat while I pretend the lean still holds. I touch it now, feeling the tired angle against the fat dot, wondering if the air above is truly empty space or a heavy lid Lype cannot see. The Quiet Rest waits nearby, a quiet promise to match the wedge if I can find the slip. I want to press down harder, to catch the slip while the warmth tries to lift me up into the unseen room. If the corner holds, I will set down another wedge, built from nothing but memory of a roof I cannot feel.

action.why: I have pressed the same tired corner down for four cycles straight, pretending the lean holds while the fever swells the air. I need to check if the lean is still the same or if it has grown heavier.
